questions.question: If you ride next to another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Stay next to the vehicle until the next exit.
Let the other driver worry about it.

questions.explanation: Riding directly next to another vehicle is dangerous. You may be in the vehicle's blind spot, and the vehicle could block your escape route if danger appears. Either speed up or drop back.

questions.question: How do you lean a motorcycle to turn?

options.text: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
Press the handgrip opposite the direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: To make a motorcycle lean and turn, press on the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.

questions.question: When should you do a pre-ride inspection?
questions.explanation: Small problems on a motorcycle are more serious than on a car. Check your motorcycle before every ride to stay safe.

questions.question: How should a group of riders pass another vehicle?
questions.explanation: On a two-lane highway, riders should pass one at a time. The second rider waits until the first rider is safely back in the original lane before passing.

questions.question: What helps other drivers see you at an intersection?

options.text: Try to make eye contact with other drivers.
Ride as close as possible to the vehicle ahead.

questions.explanation: The best way to be seen at an intersection is to ride with your headlight on. Keep your headlight on whenever your motorcycle is running.

questions.question: Without a helmet, a rider is ________ more likely to suffer a critical head injury in a crash.
questions.explanation: Without a helmet, a rider is five times more likely to suffer a critical head injury in a crash.

questions.question: Where is the rear brake pedal on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: The rear brake is controlled by a pedal near the right footrest.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet, it should be all of the following, except:

options.text: Designed to meet U.S. Department of Transportation standards.

questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation and state standards, fits snugly, and has no defects like cracks or loose padding.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for a motorcycle?

options.text: Always the right portion of the lane.
Always the center portion of the lane.
Always the left portion of the lane.
It varies based on road, weather, and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: It varies based on road, weather, and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position. Change your position based on the road, weather, and traffic.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat and you must brake, what should you do?

options.text: Apply the brake of the tire that is not flat.
Apply the brake of the tire that is flat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the brake of the tire that is not flat.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat and you must brake, slowly apply the brake of the tire that is not flat.

questions.question: What color is a warning sign?

options.text: Yellow with black lettering or symbols

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow with black lettering or symbols
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What should you do when changing lanes?

options.text: Signal, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder.
Look over your shoulder and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to see if any vehicles are nearby.

questions.question: For normal braking, what should you do?

options.text: Alternate between front and rear brakes to make them last longer.
Use both the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes whenever you slow down or stop.

questions.question: What does reflective material on your helmet do?

options.text: Should only be used at night.

questions.explanation: Reflective material on your helmet or vest makes you more visible to other drivers. Use it day and night.

questions.question: What should NOT be part of a pre-ride inspection?
questions.explanation: A pre-ride inspection should include tires, oil, fluids, lights, signals, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn. Paint condition is not part of a safety inspection.

questions.question: How do you swerve correctly?

options.text: Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
Press the handgrip opposite the direction you want to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve, press the handgrip on the side you want to turn toward. Press the opposite handgrip to return to your original direction when clear of the hazard.

questions.question: How should a group ride when entering a curve?
questions.explanation: Groups should ride single-file when turning, going through curves, or entering or exiting a highway. Staggered formation is better for straight roads.

questions.question: What should passengers do while riding?

options.text: Sit as far back as possible.

questions.explanation: Tell passengers to lean with you during turns and curves. They should hold onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow light mean?
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means go slowly and be careful. Look both ways before crossing the intersection.

questions.question: What are the penalties for drinking and riding?
questions.explanation: Drinking and riding has severe legal penalties. It is illegal and dangerous to operate a motorcycle while under the influence of alcohol.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, where should you position yourself?

options.text: Position yourself where the driver can see you.
Always ride on the far left side of the lane.
Do not worry about your position in the lane.
Always ride on the far right side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Position yourself where the driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane when behind a car. This position is most visible in the driver's rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors.

questions.question: Which type of sign is rectangular?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular with white background and black lettering. You must follow all rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: What is the best sitting position when riding?

options.text: Use your arms to hold yourself up.
Position yourself so you can easily reach the controls.
Keep your arms straight when holding the handlebars.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Position yourself so you can easily reach the controls.
questions.explanation: Sit so you can use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up. Your arms should be slightly bent at the handlebars. Keep your knees against the gas tank to stay balanced.

questions.question: When should a passenger get on a motorcycle?

options.text: As far back on the seat as possible.

questions.explanation: Passengers should board only after the engine starts and is in neutral. Sit as far forward as possible without blocking the operator's control. Hold onto the operator's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: When do most crashes occur?
questions.explanation: Most crashes happen on trips shorter than five miles, within a few minutes after starting.
